questions.question_text: Compare the structural frameworks and developmental rules of a 'Kayada' and a 'Peshkar' in a solo Tabla performance. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A Kayada follows strict mathematical rules; its variations (Paltas) must exclusively use the original bols of the main theme. A Peshkar, played at the beginning of a solo, is more flexible, allowing diverse stroke combinations to establish the groove.

questions.question_text: Briefly describe the 'Laghu', 'Drutam', and 'Anudrutam' angas (limbs) used in the Carnatic Tala system to measure rhythmic cycles. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: In Carnatic music, an Anudrutam is a single downward clap representing one beat. A Drutam is a clap followed by an empty wave, representing two beats. A Laghu is a clap followed by finger counts, with variable beats (3, 4, 5, 7, or 9) based on its Jati.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between the 'Thah' and 'Dugun' Layakaris (tempos) while reciting a Tala. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: 'Thah' or single speed involves reciting exactly one rhythmic syllable (bol) per beat (Matra) of the Tala. 'Dugun' or double speed doubles the rhythmic density, requiring the recitation of two evenly spaced syllables per beat.

questions.question_text: Explain the acoustic difference and playing technique between 'Band Baaj' (closed strokes) and 'Khula Baaj' (open strokes) in percussion instruments. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Band Baaj uses fingertips near the rim (Chati) to produce dry, crisp, non-resonating sounds, prevalent in the Delhi Gharana. Khula Baaj uses open palms and wrists to produce heavy, deep, resonating sounds, typical of the Pakhawaj and Benares Gharana.

questions.question_text: Write the structural layout grid and full notation of Ektal showing its divisions, claps (Tali), and wave hands (Khali) in Thah (Single) and Dugun (Double) speed configurations using the Bhatkhande notation system. [Notation structural format]
questions.answer:
Ektal contains 12 Matras divided into 6 equal Vibhags of 2 beats each. The structural clap points (Tali) hit on beats 1, 5, 9, and 11, while empty wave hands (Khali) are marked on beats 3 and 7.

Thah Layout:
| Dhin Dhin | DhaGe TiRkiTa | Tu Na | Kat Ta | DhaGe TiRkiTa | Dhin Na |
Sign: X (1) 0 (3) 2 (5) 0 (7) 3 (9) 4 (11)

Dugun Layout:
| DhinDhin DhaGeTiRkiTa | TuNa KatTa | DhaGeTiRkiTa DhinNa | DhinDhin DhaGeTiRkiTa | TuNa KatTa | DhaGeTiRkiTa DhinNa |

questions.question_text: Draft a biographical sketch of the legendary percussionist Ustad Ahmad Jaan Thirakwa, highlighting his foundational training, distinct playing style, and major contributions to Hindustani music. [80-100 words]
questions.answer: Ustad Ahmad Jaan Thirakwa (1892–1976) was one of the most influential Tabla maestros of the 20th century. Born in Moradabad, he received his primary training in the Farrukhabad Gharana under Ustad Munir Khan. Known for his title 'Thirakwa'—given for his fingers playfully 'dancing' on the Tabla—he mastered the repertoire of the Delhi, Ajrada, Farrukhabad, and Lucknow gharanas. He radically redefined solo Tabla performances, elevating them to an independent concert status equivalent to vocal music. His extraordinary tonal clarity, complex rhythmic variations, and ability to blend multiple Gharana styles made him an unparalleled legend in Hindustani percussion.
